ov: Tailless, short-bodied amphibians, making up about 88% of all amphibian species. Most start life as tadpoles in water, and “toads” are simply frogs with drier, wartier skin.

why.dg: Most are harmless to touch, but frog skin secretions range from distasteful to toxic, and brightly coloured species warn predators they’re poisonous.
why.et: Frogs, especially their muscular hind legs, are eaten in many parts of the world.
why.h: In colder regions many frogs hibernate through winter, and some can even survive being frozen.

rg: Worldwide, from the tropics to subarctic regions. Most species live in tropical rainforests and their wetlands.
df: Mostly insects and other invertebrates, caught with a sticky tongue and swallowed whole. A few species eat plants.

cf.tip: Toads are frogs with drier, rougher, wartier skin that live more on land. The split is informal and doesn’t match scientific classification.

fx: The oldest known “proto-frog” lived in Madagascar about 250 million years ago.
